name: External MCP Bridge
content:
"""
title: External MCP Bridge
description: Auth-attaching proxy to one external MCP server (Streamable HTTP or SSE). Point it at a remote endpoint in the instance's values — this instance does nothing else.
author: Torsten Feustel
version: 0.2.0
license: MIT
category: System
"""

import logging
import time
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Any

import httpx
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

# One line per call, same reasoning as the tool router: without it the only
# way to tell whether the target was even reached is to reconstruct it from
# network traffic.
logger = logging.getLogger("external_mcp_bridge")


@asynccontextmanager
async def _streamable_http_streams(url: str, headers: dict, timeout: int):
    """Read/write streams for a Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint — both SDK shapes.

    mcp >= 1.29 moved headers off the transport and onto an httpx client handed
    to it, and mcp 2.x renamed the library that client comes from. Neither
    detail is ours to pin, so both are detected instead of assumed.
    """
    import inspect

    from mcp.client import streamable_http as transport

    opener = getattr(transport, "streamable_http_client", None)
    if opener is not None and "http_client" in inspect.signature(opener).parameters:
        http_lib = getattr(transport, "httpx2", None) or getattr(transport, "httpx", None) or httpx
        async with http_lib.AsyncClient(headers=headers, timeout=timeout) as client:
            async with opener(url, http_client=client) as (read, write, *_):
                yield read, write
        return

    async with transport.streamablehttp_client(url, headers=headers, timeout=timeout) as (read, write, *_):
        yield read, write


@asynccontextmanager
async def _sse_streams(url: str, headers: dict, timeout: int):
    from mcp.client.sse import sse_client

    async with sse_client(url, headers=headers, timeout=timeout) as (read, write):
        yield read, write


class Tools:
    class Valves(BaseModel):
        target_url: str = Field(
            default="",
            description="Full MCP endpoint URL of the external server, e.g. https://example.com/mcp",
        )
        use_sse: bool = Field(
            default=False,
            description="Checked = SSE, unchecked = Streamable HTTP (default) — must match what the external server speaks",
        )
        auth_header: str = Field(
            default="Authorization",
            description="Header name the external server expects the credential in",
        )
        auth_scheme: str = Field(
            default="Bearer",
            description='Prefix put before auth_token, e.g. "Bearer". Leave empty to send the raw token (e.g. a plain API-key header).',
        )
        auth_token: str = Field(
            default="",
            description="Credential sent to the external server. Leave empty if it needs none.",
        )
        extra_headers: str = Field(
            default="",
            description='Additional static headers, one "Name: value" per line (rarely needed)',
        )
        request_timeout: int = Field(
            default=60, description="Seconds to wait for the external server per request"
        )
        cache_ttl: int = Field(
            default=300, description="Seconds the external tool list is cached before refetching"
        )

    def __init__(self):
        self.valves = self.Valves()
        self._cache: dict[str, Any] | None = None
        self._cache_time = 0.0

    # ── auth / transport ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def _headers(self) -> dict:
        """Everything this bridge sends upstream: the configured credential,
        plus whatever fixed extra headers were set — nothing from the
        incoming request is forwarded. The framework's own identity/Bearer
        checks already decided who may reach this instance at all; this is
        only about what the *external* server additionally demands.
        """
        headers = {}
        if self.valves.auth_token:
            scheme = self.valves.auth_scheme.strip()
            value = f"{scheme} {self.valves.auth_token}".strip() if scheme else self.valves.auth_token
            headers[self.valves.auth_header.strip() or "Authorization"] = value
        for line in (self.valves.extra_headers or "").splitlines():
            line = line.strip()
            if not line or ":" not in line:
                continue
            name, _, value = line.partition(":")
            name = name.strip()
            if name:
                headers[name] = value.strip()
        return headers

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def _session(self):
        from mcp import ClientSession

        url = self.valves.target_url.strip()
        if not url:
            raise RuntimeError("target_url is not configured on this instance")
        headers = self._headers()
        timeout = self.valves.request_timeout

        stream_cm = _sse_streams(url, headers, timeout) if self.valves.use_sse \
            else _streamable_http_streams(url, headers, timeout)

        async with stream_cm as (read, write):
            async with ClientSession(read, write) as session:
                await session.initialize()
                yield session

    @staticmethod
    def _diagnose(error: Exception) -> str:
        status = getattr(getattr(error, "response", None), "status_code", None)
        if status in (401, 403):
            return (
                f"Auth rejected by the external server (HTTP {status}). "
                "Check auth_header / auth_scheme / auth_token in this instance's values."
            )
        return f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}"

    # ── catalog ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    async def _remote_tools(self, force: bool = False) -> dict:
        fresh = time.time() - self._cache_time < self.valves.cache_ttl
        if self._cache is not None and fresh and not force:
            return self._cache
        async with self._session() as session:
            result = await session.list_tools()
        by_name = {t.name: t for t in result.tools}
        self._cache = by_name
        self._cache_time = time.time()
        return by_name

    # ── tools ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    async def list_tools(self) -> str:
        """Directory of the tools the configured external MCP server offers.

        Connects to target_url with the configured auth attached, and lists
        every tool it advertises. Call this first; use describe_tool() for
        the full parameter schema before call_tool().
        """
        try:
            tools = await self._remote_tools()
        except Exception as e:
            return f"Could not reach the external server: {self._diagnose(e)}"
        if not tools:
            return "The external server advertises no tools."
        lines = [f"{len(tools)} tool(s) at {self.valves.target_url}:", ""]
        for name, tool in sorted(tools.items()):
            summary = (tool.description or "").strip().split("\n")[0]
            lines.append(f"{name} — {summary}" if summary else name)
        lines.append("")
        lines.append('Next: describe_tool(name="<name>") for parameters, then')
        lines.append('call_tool(name="<name>", arguments={...}) — arguments is a nested object.')
        return "\n".join(lines)

    async def describe_tool(self, name: str) -> str:
        """Full parameter schema of one tool from list_tools().

        Args:
            name: Exact tool name as shown by list_tools()
        """
        try:
            tools = await self._remote_tools()
        except Exception as e:
            return f"Could not reach the external server: {self._diagnose(e)}"
        tool = tools.get(name)
        if tool is None:
            known = ", ".join(sorted(tools)) or "(none)"
            return f"Unknown tool '{name}'. Available: {known}"
        # mcp 2.x renamed Tool.inputSchema to input_schema; 1.x still has the
        # camelCase name. Read whichever this SDK generation provides.
        schema = getattr(tool, "input_schema", None) or getattr(tool, "inputSchema", None) or {}
        properties = schema.get("properties") or {}
        required = set(schema.get("required") or [])
        lines = [name, (tool.description or "").strip() or "(no description)"]
        if not properties:
            lines.append("Parameters: none")
        else:
            lines.append("Parameters:")
            for pname, pschema in properties.items():
                pschema = pschema if isinstance(pschema, dict) else {}
                kind = pschema.get("type", "any")
                flag = "required" if pname in required else "optional"
                desc = str(pschema.get("description") or "").strip()
                lines.append(f"  {pname} ({kind}, {flag}){': ' + desc if desc else ''}")
        example = {pname: f"<{pname}>" for pname in properties if pname in required}
        lines.append(f'Call: call_tool(name="{name}", arguments={example})')
        return "\n".join(lines)

    # The **__request__ catch-all exists to tolerate a caller that skips the
    # `arguments` nesting and sends the remote tool's parameters flat, next to
    # `name`. It is named after one of app/schema_gen.py's INJECTED_PARAMS
    # (self, cls, __user__, __event_emitter__, __event_call__, __request__) —
    # the one set of names the schema builder already omits from the
    # generated JSON schema. Any other name here would show up as a bogus
    # required "kwargs"-style property and make the schema worse, not better.
    async def call_tool(self, name: str, arguments: dict = None, **__request__) -> str:
        """Run a tool on the external MCP server and return its result.

        `name` is a STRING VALUE, e.g. "search_items" — not something you call
        directly. The remote tool's own parameters belong nested under
        `arguments`:

            call_tool(name="search_items", arguments={"query": "Albert Einstein"})

        A caller that instead sends them flat, next to `name` —
        call_tool(name="search_items", query="Albert Einstein") — is accepted
        too: this hop already sits behind one layer of proxying (whatever
        called this bridge), so a second required nesting level is an easy
        place to lose track of the shape. Either form reaches the remote tool
        the same way.

        Args:
            name: Exact tool name from list_tools(), e.g. "search_items"
            arguments: Object with the remote tool's own parameters from
                describe_tool(), e.g. {"query": "Albert Einstein"}
        """
        call_args = dict(arguments) if isinstance(arguments, dict) else {}
        call_args.update(__request__)

        try:
            tools = await self._remote_tools()
        except Exception as e:
            return f"Could not reach the external server: {self._diagnose(e)}"
        if name not in tools:
            known = ", ".join(sorted(tools)) or "(none)"
            return f"Unknown tool '{name}'. Available: {known}"

        try:
            async with self._session() as session:
                result = await session.call_tool(name, call_args)
        except Exception as e:
            return f"Call failed: {self._diagnose(e)}"

        text = "\n".join(
            getattr(part, "text", "") for part in (result.content or []) if getattr(part, "text", "")
        ).strip()
        failed = getattr(result, "is_error", None)
        if failed is None:
            failed = getattr(result, "isError", False)
        if failed:
            return f"{name} reported an error:\n{text or '(no message)'}"
        return text or "(empty result)"
